baseline_facts.content: Patient date of birth is 31 October 1990.
Patient reports decreased hearing in the left ear.
Decreased hearing has been present for about six weeks.
Patient had a brief hearing problem about a year ago lasting a couple of days.
Patient occasionally experiences ringing in the left ear.
Patient has felt slightly sick at times during the last six weeks.
Dizziness is not severe.
Dizziness described as feeling off balance.
Dizziness is not associated with room-spinning.
Dizziness is not associated with nausea.
Patient denies chest pain.
Patient denies ear pain in the left ear.
Patient denies hearing difficulty in the right ear.
Patient does not use cotton buds to clean ears.
Face-to-face ear examination is planned within the next four to five days.
The condition is not considered an emergency.
Planned ear examination aims to exclude impacted ear wax.
Doctor identified the ringing as tinnitus.
Doctor planned to provide a leaflet link about tinnitus.
Doctor advised against using cotton buds to clean ear wax.

candidate_facts.content: Left ear hearing loss.
Intermittent tinnitus in the left ear.
Mild dizziness.
Left ear hearing loss began about 6 weeks ago.
Prior ear-related event about a year ago lasting a couple of days.
Watching TV seems to reduce the ringing.
Listening to music seems to reduce the ringing.
No ear pain.
No ear discharge.
No fever.
Dizziness is not spinning.
Dizziness is not associated with nausea.
Dizziness events were on and off over 6 weeks.
Dizziness can be triggered.
No chest pain.
No palpitations.
Patient does not use cotton buds for ear cleaning.
Plan to exclude cerumen impaction before other etiologies.
Ear examination by a GP is planned.
In-clinic ear examination scheduled within ~4–5 days.
No medications were prescribed at this time.
Patient to monitor for progression or new symptoms.
Patient advised to seek urgent care if fever develops.
Patient advised to seek urgent care if severe vertigo occurs.
Patient advised to seek urgent care if persistent ear pain occurs.
Patient advised to seek urgent care if otorrhea occurs.
Patient advised to seek urgent care if worsening hearing occurs.
No ENT consult is planned at this time.
Notes and plan will be reviewed by another GP during the scheduled clinic visit.
Patient will be provided a link to a tinnitus leaflet to read before the appointment.
Condition categorized as non-emergency.
Patient advised to attend the clinic appointment.
Patient advised to contact support to schedule.
Cerumen impaction causing muffled hearing is a differential diagnosis.
Other middle or inner ear pathology affecting hearing or balance is a differential consideration.
Sensorineural hearing loss is considered less likely.
A vestibular or inner ear disorder contributing to dizziness is a differential consideration.
Eustachian tube dysfunction is a differential consideration.
If wax impaction is found, management will follow ear exam findings.
